requirements.text: The business must be able to identify each employee uniquely and consistently across all HR reporting.
Each employee carries a national identification number (such as a social security number), described in the source system as unique, which is the strongest natural business identifier for a person.
Each employee is registered under a company-wide business entity number that is shared with a broader business-entity register outside the HR area.
The warehouse must be able to reconcile the HR view of a person with the wider business-entity register.
Each employee has a network login identifying them in company IT systems; it may be used to join HR data to system-generated activity but must not be treated as the business identity of the person.
The technical row identifier used for data replication carries no business meaning and is not required for reporting.
The business must record the job title of each employee.
The business must record the hire date of each employee.
The business must be able to derive tenure (length of service) from the hire date.
The business must record whether each employee is salaried or hourly.
Salaried staff are exempt from collective bargaining and hourly staff are not.
Reporting must be able to distinguish salaried and hourly populations for both cost and labour-relations purposes.
The business must record whether each employee is currently active or inactive, as the operational statement of whether the person is presently employed.
Headcount reporting must be able to count only active employees, only inactive employees, or all people ever employed.
The business must record the date of birth of each employee to support age-profile and workforce-planning analysis.
The business must record the gender of each employee (male or female in the source).
The business must record the marital status of each employee (married or single in the source).
Access to date of birth, gender and marital status in the warehouse must be restricted to authorised HR users.
Reporting for a wider audience must be possible without exposing date of birth, gender or marital status, for example by using age bands rather than birth dates.
The exact restrictions on personal data require a data-protection review.
The business must record the available vacation hours of each employee.
The business must record the available sick leave hours of each employee.
Leave balances are remaining entitlements at a point in time, not accruals or consumption transactions, and reporting must be clear about the date to which any stated balance applies.
The business must be able to see how leave balances have moved over time, as a series of balance readings, to identify unusually high accrued balances and their associated liability.
The business must record where each employee sits in the corporate hierarchy, i.e. who reports to whom.
The business must record the depth (level) of each employee in the hierarchy so reporting can distinguish senior levels from front-line staff and aggregate to any chosen level.
The business must be able to determine how many people report directly to a given manager and how many report to them in total at all levels below.
requirements.obj: spans of control and reporting lines

requirements.text: The business must be able to see the reporting structure as it stands today and, where the record permits, as it stood previously, by capturing changes as they occur.
The source only carries the current hierarchy position for each employee, so reconstruction of past structures depends on capturing changes as they occur.
The business must maintain a register of departments, the organisational units in which people work.
Each department is known by its name.
Each department belongs to a group, a larger organisational area, identified by the group's name.
Reporting must be able to aggregate any departmental measure (headcount, pay, movement) to the group level.
Departments can be created or retired, and department names and group memberships can be changed.
The business must know when a department's details were last changed.

The business would like to see figures both on today's departmental structure and on the structure in force at the time, which requires history to be captured since the source holds only the current department description.
requirements.obj: figures by current and historical departmental structure

requirements.text: The business must maintain a register of working shifts, each representing an eight-hour working period.
Each shift is known by its name (shift description).
The business must record the start time and end time of each shift.
Reporting must be able to analyse the workforce by shift, for example how many people work each shift, in which departments, and how that has changed.
Shift definitions (name, start time, end time) can be adjusted.

Where a shift's times change, the business must be able to understand that a person recorded on a shift in the past may have worked different hours than someone recorded on the same-named shift today.
The business must record, for each employee, which department they worked in and on which shift, over time.
Each department and shift assignment must remain visible after it ends.
Each assignment records the date the employee started work in the department.
Each assignment records the date the employee left the department.
An assignment with no recorded leaving date is the employee's current department assignment.
The business must be able to reliably identify current assignments on the basis of a missing leaving date.
The business must be able to state, for any given date in the past, which department and shift an employee was working in.
requirements.obj: employee department and shift at a past date

requirements.text: The business must be able to produce headcount by department at any point in time, not merely today.
requirements.obj: headcount by department at a point in time

requirements.text: The business must be able to report movement between departments (transfers in, transfers out and net change) for any period, by department and by group.
The business must be able to report movement between shifts (transfers in, transfers out and net change) for any period, by shift and by group.
The business must be able to measure how long an employee spends in a department before moving.
requirements.obj: length of employee assignment in a department

requirements.text: The business must be able to report the average length of assignment by department and by group.
An employee may have held the same department more than once at different times, for example leaving and later returning.
Reporting must treat repeated stays in the same department as separate assignments rather than merging them.
In the source, an individual assignment is recognised by the combination of employee, department, shift and start date.
The business must record the pay rate of each employee and how it has changed over time.
Each change in an employee's pay rate, which occurs on defined dates, must remain visible.
Each pay record carries the date on which the change in pay becomes effective, not the date the record was entered.
Each pay record carries the rate, expressed as an hourly rate in money terms.
Each pay record carries the pay frequency, which is either monthly or biweekly.
Pay frequency must be available for cost-phasing and payroll-cycle analysis.
requirements.obj: cost phasing and payroll cycle using pay frequency

requirements.text: The business must be able to state an employee's rate as at any given date, using the rate whose effective date was most recent on or before that date.
requirements.obj: employee pay rate at a given date

requirements.text: The business must be able to report pay progression for an individual: the sequence of rates, the size of each change, and the interval between changes.
The business must be able to report average, minimum and maximum rates by department, group, job title, shift and salaried/hourly classification, at a chosen point in time.
requirements.obj: average, minimum and maximum pay rates

requirements.text: The business must be able to combine pay history with departmental assignment history so that a rate is attributed to the department the employee was working in when it applied.
requirements.obj: pay history with department assignment history

requirements.text: The business must be able to analyse pay differences across groups of employees, such as between job titles or departments, in support of pay-equity review.
Any pay analysis touching gender or other personal attributes is subject to the access restrictions in REQ-015 of the source document.
The conversion from an hourly rate to a periodic cost must be confirmed with Payroll before any cost figure is published.
The business must record job candidates, being people who applied for a position and whose application is held by HR.
Each candidate record carries the candidate's résumé, held as a structured document rather than as separate fields.
The business must be able to know that a candidate's résumé exists and to retrieve it.
A candidate record may be linked to an employee, and that link means the applicant was hired.
A candidate with no linked employee was not hired, or has not been hired yet.
The business must be able to report hiring outcomes: how many candidates were recorded, how many were subsequently employed, and the conversion rate between the two.
The business must be able to trace an employed person back to the candidate record that preceded their employment, where one exists.
Not every employee has a candidate record; employees with no application on file are permitted.
Retention and access rules for candidate personal data must be established before this data is published.
Recruitment-funnel reporting beyond the hired/not-hired outcome is not supported, because the source does not record the position applied for, application date or rejection reason.
Every record in this area carries the date and time it was last updated in the operational system.
The business must be able to tell how current a given piece of information is and identify records that have not been touched for an unexpectedly long time.
requirements.obj: stale records based on last-updated timestamp

requirements.text: Changes the source system keeps a history of, namely departmental and shift assignments and pay rates, must be distinguished from other changes, since their past is recoverable from the source.

Changes the source system overwrites, namely job title, marital status, leave balances, active/inactive status, position in the hierarchy, and department and shift descriptions, must be distinguished as having only a current value in the source.

For the overwritten attributes, the warehouse must preserve the succession of values by observing changes as they occur, so that questions such as how many people held a given job title at the end of last year become answerable in future.
requirements.obj: succession of values of overwritten attributes

requirements.text: Reporting must clearly distinguish as-is figures, using today's department structure and employee attributes, from as-was figures, using the structure and attributes in force at the time.
The business must be able to reproduce a previously published figure, so that re-running a report issued for a period gives the same answer notwithstanding later corrections to the source.
The business must be able to produce headcount and full-time-equivalent style summaries by department, group, shift, job title and salaried/hourly classification, at a chosen date.
The business must be able to report joiners and leavers by period, derived from hire dates and from the ending of assignments and the active/inactive status.
The business must be able to report tenure and age profiles of the workforce in bands.
The business must be able to report internal mobility: how many people changed department or shift in a period, and the flows between specific departments.
The business must be able to report pay-rate distribution and progression by department, group, job title, shift and salaried/hourly classification.
The business must be able to report accrued vacation and sick-leave balances by department and group as an indicator of liability.
The business must be able to report recruitment conversion as the relationship between candidates recorded and candidates subsequently employed.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 describes the national identification number as unique and the strongest natural business identifier for a person; REQ-001 requires unique, consistent identification. It is stable, business-recognised and carried by every employee.

REQ-003 says each employee is registered under a company-wide business entity number shared with a wider register, and REQ-004 requires reconciliation with that register. It is unique and used by the business, but it is a cross-domain register number rather than the person's own identifier, so it ranks below the national ID.
REQ-005 says the network login may be used to join to system activity but must not be treated as the person's business identity. It can change and is a weak key.

REQ-030 requires a department register, and the source has a DepartmentID. The requirements do not call it the business identifier, and it looks system-assigned, so confidence is moderate. It is also used in the assignment key in REQ-015-2.
REQ-031 states each department is known by its name, so the business recognises it. REQ-034 says names can change, which weakens stability, and uniqueness is not stated.

REQ-037 requires a shift register, and ShiftID is part of the assignment key in REQ-015-2. The requirements do not state it as the business identifier, and it looks system-assigned, so confidence is moderate.
REQ-038 states each shift is known by its name. REQ-041 and REQ-042 say definitions can be adjusted and same-named shifts can differ over time, so stability and uniqueness are uncertain.

REQ-015-2 states an individual assignment is recognised in the source by the combination of employee, department, shift and start date. REQ-013-2 and REQ-014-2 require repeat stays to be separate assignments, which the start date allows. This composite is a strong key for the assignment relationship.

REQ-016-2 to REQ-018-2 say each pay change is a record on an effective date, and REQ-022-2 selects the rate by most recent effective date. The employee plus effective date identifies one pay record. The requirements do not state this key explicitly.

REQ-029-2 requires candidate records, but no business-assigned identifier is mentioned. JobCandidateID is the only listed candidate identifier and looks system-generated, so it is a weak key but is needed to anchor candidates.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_leave
satellites.description: Leave balances (vacation and sick-leave hours remaining). The satellite builds a history of balance readings over time.
satellites.split_rationale: Leave balances change much more often than other employee attributes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy
satellites.description: The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. History builds up as changes are captured.
satellites.split_rationale: Hierarchy position changes at its own rate and is used for reporting-line analysis.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_employee_pay
satellites.description: Pay-rate history per employee: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and the pay frequency.
satellites.split_rationale: Comes from its own source relation at a finer grain (employee + RateChangeDate), and the source keeps its history. EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity so this binding is valid.

satellites.name: sat_department_details
satellites.description: Department group membership and last-change timestamp. History is captured over time to support as-was reporting.

satellites.name: sat_shift_details
satellites.description: Shift start and end times. Captured historically because shift definitions can be adjusted.

satellites.name: sat_job_candidate_details
satellites.description: The candidate's résumé (a structured document) and the last-modified timestamp.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity
satellites.description: Active period of each department/shift assignment. A missing EndDate marks the current assignment.

contracts.name: Department

schema.name: DepartmentID

schema.name: Name

contracts.name: Employee

schema.name: BusinessEntityID

schema.name: NationalIDNumber

schema.name: LoginID

schema.name: OrganizationNode

schema.name: OrganizationLevel

schema.name: JobTitle

schema.name: BirthDate
schema.description: Employee's date of birth.

schema.name: MaritalStatus
schema.description: Marital status code of the employee.

schema.name: Gender
schema.description: Gender code of the employee.

schema.name: HireDate
schema.description: Date the employee was hired.

schema.name: SalariedFlag
schema.description: Indicates whether the employee is salaried (as opposed to hourly) .

schema.name: VacationHours
schema.description: Number of vacation hours available to the employee.

schema.name: SickLeaveHours
schema.description: Number of sick leave hours available to the employee.

schema.name: CurrentFlag
schema.description: Indicates whether the employee record is currently active.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the source row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: EmployeeDepartmentHistory
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset recording the history of an employee's assignments to departments and shifts over time, with start and end dates for each assignment. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity; value-level constraints are limited to those grounded in stated requirements. Ownership and agreement status are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the employee (business entity) assigned to the department; refers to the Employee's BusinessEntityID.

schema.name: DepartmentID
schema.description: Identifier of the department the employee was assigned to; refers to the Department's DepartmentID.

schema.name: ShiftID
schema.description: Identifier of the shift the employee worked during the assignment; refers to the Shift's ShiftID.

schema.name: StartDate
schema.description: Date the employee started the assignment in the department and shift.

schema.name: EndDate
schema.description: Date the employee's assignment in the department and shift ended; may be empty for a current assignment.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: EmployeePayHistory
contracts.doc: Staging asset for employee pay history: one record per employee per pay rate change, capturing the effective date of the change, the new rate and its pay frequency. The contract enforces the declared schema, business-key uniqueness and not-null rules; no value-level thresholds are mandated by the requirements.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the employee whose pay rate changed; references the Employee entity (BusinessEntityID).

schema.name: RateChangeDate
schema.description: Date on which the employee's pay rate change took effect.

schema.name: Rate
schema.description: Pay rate assigned to the employee as of the rate change date. Currency and unit are not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: PayFrequency
schema.description: Code indicating how often the employee is paid. The allowed value set and code meanings are not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: JobCandidate
contracts.doc: Staging asset for job candidates from the source HR JobCandidate table. The contract enforces schema, primary key and not-null rules; no further value-level constraints are stated in the requirements.

schema.name: JobCandidateID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the job candidate record in the source system.

schema.name: Resume

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source system.

schema.name: Name

schema.name: StartTime

schema.name: EndTime

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 94 requirement(s) and 10 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (3)

- **hub_department** — business key `Name`. Register of departments, the organisational units people work in, keyed on department name (agreed decided key). _(requirements: REQ-030, REQ-031, REQ-034)_
- **hub_shift** — business key `Name`. Register of eight-hour working shifts, keyed on shift name (agreed decided key). _(requirements: REQ-037, REQ-038)_
- **hub_job_candidate** — business key `JobCandidateID`. Job candidates: people who applied for a position and whose application is held by HR. _(requirements: REQ-029-2, REQ-034-2, REQ-052)_

### Links (2)

- **link_business_entity_department_shift** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_department, hub_shift. Employee assignment to a department and shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. Supports headcount at a point in time, mobility and movement reporting, and tracking how long an employee stays in an assignment. Unit of work: BusinessEntityID + DepartmentID + ShiftID (one assignment, starting on StartDate). Driving key: hub_business_entity. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-002-2, REQ-007-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-010-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-040, REQ-049)_
- **link_job_candidate_business_entity** — connects hub_job_candidate, hub_business_entity. Links a candidate record to the employee hired from it. A candidate with no link was not hired, or has not been hired yet. Unit of work: JobCandidateID + BusinessEntityID (hire of a candidate). _(requirements: REQ-032-2, REQ-033-2, REQ-035-2, REQ-036-2, REQ-034-2)_

### Satellites (9)

- **sat_business_entity_employee_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: JobTitle, HireDate, SalariedFlag, CurrentFlag, LoginID, ModifiedDate. Employee job and employment-status attributes: job title, hire date, salaried/hourly flag, active/inactive flag, network login, and the last-modified timestamp. Source table: Employee. Split rationale: Employment attributes that are not sensitive and change slowly. ModifiedDate is kept only here. rowguid is left out because it has no business meaning (REQ-006).. _(requirements: REQ-005, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-039-2, REQ-040-2, REQ-043)_
- **sat_business_entity_employee_sensitive** — on hub_business_entity; payload: NationalIDNumber, BirthDate, Gender, MaritalStatus. Restricted personal data about employees: national ID number, date of birth, gender and marital status. Source table: Employee. Split rationale: Split out by data classification (PII), so access can be restricted to authorised HR users.. _(requirements: REQ-002, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020)_
- **sat_business_entity_employee_leave** — on hub_business_entity; payload: VacationHours, SickLeaveHours. Leave balances (vacation and sick-leave hours remaining). The satellite builds a history of balance readings over time. Source table: Employee. Split rationale: Leave balances change much more often than other employee attributes.. _(requirements: REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-051)_
- **sat_business_entity_employee_hierarchy** — on hub_business_entity; payload: OrganizationNode, OrganizationLevel. The employee's position and level in the corporate hierarchy. History builds up as changes are captured. Source table: Employee. Split rationale: Hierarchy position changes at its own rate and is used for reporting-line analysis.. _(requirements: REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-027, REQ-028, REQ-029)_
- **sat_business_entity_employee_pay** — on hub_business_entity; payload: Rate, PayFrequency, ModifiedDate. Pay-rate history per employee: one row per effective rate-change date, with the hourly rate and the pay frequency. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: RateChangeDate. Source table: EmployeePayHistory. Split rationale: Comes from its own source relation at a finer grain (employee + RateChangeDate), and the source keeps its history. EmployeePayHistory is now declared as a feed of hub_business_entity so this binding is valid.. _(requirements: REQ-016-2, REQ-017-2, REQ-018-2, REQ-019-2, REQ-020-2, REQ-021-2, REQ-022-2, REQ-023-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-050)_
- **sat_department_details** — on hub_department; payload: GroupName, ModifiedDate. Department group membership and last-change timestamp. History is captured over time to support as-was reporting. Source table: Department. _(requirements: REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035, REQ-036, REQ-044)_
- **sat_shift_details** — on hub_shift; payload: StartTime, EndTime, ModifiedDate. Shift start and end times. Captured historically because shift definitions can be adjusted. Source table: Shift. _(requirements: REQ-039, REQ-041, REQ-042)_
- **sat_job_candidate_details** — on hub_job_candidate; payload: Resume, ModifiedDate. The candidate's résumé (a structured document) and the last-modified timestamp. Source table: JobCandidate. _(requirements: REQ-030-2, REQ-031-2, REQ-037-2, REQ-039-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_department_shift_effectivity** — on link_business_entity_department_shift; payload: StartDate, EndDate. Active period of each department/shift assignment. A missing EndDate marks the current assignment. Effectivity satellite. Source table: EmployeeDepartmentHistory. _(requirements: REQ-003-2, REQ-004-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-006-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-025-2)_
